conceptual assets.information: Register operands, the third operand, and selected immediate or current-PC values are consumed by the ALU and coprocessor operations. Only derived values leave the unit, rather than an operand being returned unchanged.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: These values may contain private execution data, and the RTL exposes functions of them through res_o, add_o, cmp_o, and the child-operation result paths (97-108, 119, 129-135, 176, 199, 235, 268, 372, 406).
conceptual assets.attack: An observer could use the result or comparison outputs to infer supplied operand values or relationships between them.

conceptual assets.information: Arithmetic, logical, and coprocessor operation results are computed and returned for execution and write-back use. The result paths include the dedicated adder output and the selected result output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The results can contain private operand-derived data and leave through add_o or res_o (119, 129-135); internal result computation or the black-box coprocessor outputs can alter them (116-117, 176, 199, 235, 268, 313, 335, 372, 406). The result can be selected as zero or withheld by operation selection and coprocessor-valid/active gating (126-136, 334-343).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt operation selection or result-valid gating to disclose derived data, return an incorrect result, or replace a requested result with zero.

conceptual assets.information: Equality and signed or unsigned less-than comparison results are computed from the first two operands. The outcome is both returned and supplied to selected coprocessor operations.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: cmp_o directly exposes an equality or ordering relationship between operand values (100-102). The comparator result is produced by internal logic and can be made incorrect through its operand interpretation and comparator paths (97-101).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe cmp_o to learn a relationship between private operands or corrupt the comparison used by a dependent operation.

conceptual assets.information: Valid and completion indications from the optional coprocessor operations determine whether an operation has completed and whether its result is presented as done. The status is combined into done_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Incorrect child valid signals or the aggregation into done_o can report completion at the wrong time and corrupt operation sequencing (147, 177, 200, 236, 269, 314, 343, 373, 407). Suppressing cp_valid suppresses done_o and can leave a dependent operation waiting or discard its result (147, 343).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could suppress or forge a completion indication so the processor waits indefinitely, accepts an unfinished result, or loses a completed result.

conceptual assets.information: Control and status register contents held by the optional FPU and custom-function coprocessor affect those operations and are returned through the CSR readback path. CSR writes enter the child instances and their read data is merged onto csr_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: CSR contents can include sensitive operation state and are exposed through child read-data outputs and csr_o (261, 275, 304, 320, 155). The child CSR state can be changed by the forwarded write enable, address, and data inputs (258-260, 301-303), under the black-box instance rule.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe csr_o or inject a CSR write to disclose or corrupt coprocessor configuration and status.

conceptual assets.information: The clocked CFU busy state records whether a custom-function operation is active and controls when its result and valid indication are accepted. It is internal state and has no direct output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: cfu_busy is set, cleared, and reset as operation state and controls cfu_active, cp_result capture, and cp_valid (325-343), so unauthorized modification can accept the wrong result or corrupt the operation state. A stuck busy or premature clear can respectively block or discard a CFU result (329-343).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the busy state to remain set or clear early, preventing a custom operation from completing or accepting an unrelated result.

conceptual assets.information: Address-decoded CSR enable and write-enable decisions determine whether FPU or CFU CSR accesses are accepted and whether selected readback data is released. This decision is separate from the CSR contents themselves.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The decoded enables control child CSR writes and gate the data returned to csr_o (273-275, 318-320), so changing them can redirect or authorize an unintended write. Forcing either enable inactive can block CSR reads or writes needed by the selected coprocessor access (274-275, 319-320).
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the CSR address decode to expose the wrong status, block a required access, or enable a write to an unintended coprocessor CSR.

considered, not kept.reason: These are build-time feature and implementation choices, so no RTL element can change or withhold them at run time.
Clock and reset inputs and their reset propagation are explicitly excluded from conceptual assets by the clock-and-reset rule.
